content:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] Unusual routing pattern: multiple tenants on hosted plan are being routed to Dedicated pool unexpectedly. Rate of affected requests rising. auto-escalate=on :rotating_light:
oncall-alex: acked. Paging L4. tagging @sre-miguel
sre-miguel: seeing a spike in errors + 502s in dedicated backends for those tenant IDs. quick check: are we seeing cross-tenant affinity or just wrong capacity-tier mapping?
platform-ashwin: initial trace shows policy engine matched fallback rule 'tier_preference' incorrectly for requests with tenant.metadata.beta=true. looks like a policy rewrite during the rollout of routing-policy:v3 earlier today.
customer-success-zoe: we have two paying customers reporting latency and 5xxs. one is on hosted plan (acct: acme-inc). they just escalated.
daphne: any chance this is a KV cache key collision? last time that caused tenant bleed it was a prefix bug.
sre-miguel: not a cache key. logs show explicit route target: pool=dedicated:gpu-7, route_reason=fallback-policy, policy_id=rp:v3:2026-03-15. requests carry tenant_id as expected.
oncall-alex: mitigation idea: disable cross-tier fallback entirely until we patch rp:v3. can someone push a guarded config change?
platform-ashwin: I can flip the flag, but need a quick rollback plan. changing global fallback to false will force strict isolation; we might see increased latency for some long-tail requests but avoids wrong pool routing.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by platform-ashwin: apply config routing/feature_flags/fallback_cross_tier=false (canary 1 -> 10%).
incidents-bot: deploy progress: canary 1 complete, canary 10% in progress. monitoring for error increase.
sre-miguel: canary looks clean for the targeted tenants. 502s down to baseline for acme-inc.
platform-ashwin: rolling to 100% now. command: ```
# apply via control-plane
PATCH /api/v1/config/routing
{
  "fallback_cross_tier": false,
  "policy_rollout": "hold"
}
```
oncall-alex: good. notify CS and ops. Zoe, send a quick note to affected customers: "we've applied a mitigation; traffic restored to hosted pools; root cause investigation ongoing."
customer-success-zoe: message sent to acme-inc + beta customers. they confirmed lower latency. thanks. :thumbsup:
sre-miguel: quick post-check: found the policy diff that caused misassignment. snippet below where an earlier condition was promoted above tenant_isolation: true.
```yaml
# bad diff in rp:v3
- conditions:
  - tenant.metadata.beta == true -> route: prefer_dedicated
  - tenant_isolation: true
# intended order should guard tenant_isolation first
```
platform-ashwin: that explains it. config ordering bug during rollout. rp:v3 had a rebase that changed rule priority.
daphne: what's the customer impact window? need to track SLA hit and seats affected.
sre-miguel: preliminary numbers: ~2.3k requests/min affected across 7 hosted tenants over 18 minutes. peak error rate added ~1.8% error budget burn for customers on hosted plan.
oncall-alex: we'll escalate to P0 for tracking and RFC. assign owners: root cause owner=platform-ashwin, mitigation owner=sre-miguel, customer comms=customer-success-zoe.
incidents-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1837, severity=P0, runbook=https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1837
platform-ashwin: next steps: revert rp:v3 rollout, add unit/regression test for rule priority, add canary gate to prevent policy rebase from changing priority.
sre-miguel: I'll prepare a quick scrub and collect logs for a post-incident report. saving the extracted traces to s3://redwood-incidents/1851234567/traces.tar.gz
oncall-alex: handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. @daphne please take on-call for postmortem coordination and SLA calc.
daphne: taking it. I'll sync with Zoe for customer-facing timeline and with Ashwin for the deploy/RFC.
incidents-bot: update: mitigation applied cluster-wide, metric baselines restored. monitoring will remain on high for 2 hours.
customer-success-zoe: flagged to enterprise accounts team; they want an exec summary. will attach the incident link and timeline when ready.
platform-ashwin: created PR to enforce explicit priority in policy DSL and added an E2E canary check. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/routing/pulls/3421
incidents-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. will rotate to postmortem in 2 hours if stable.
end of thread."
